name: codevis
desc: Turns your code into one large image
why: Renders an entire codebase as one large image, turning source files into a strange visual map of structure.

brief.what_it_is: codevis is a command-line tool that takes every source code or UTF-8 encodable file in a folder and renders them all into one large image. It syntax-highlights files it recognizes. The output shows the shape and size of files rather than the exact characters, though a readable mode lets you zoom in and read the text.
brief.why_it_exists: The README does not state a motivation beyond the tool's output: images that show the shape and size of a codebase. It points to sister projects, codemov (video output) and codevis-gui, for related formats.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the internals. It describes a single pass over a folder that renders each file into one image. Flags seen include --bg-pixel-color, --readable, --line-nums and --show-filenames, and --help lists more options.

commands_seen.context: Visualizes all files in the current directory and subdirectories, writing to ./output.png by default.
Same as above but writes the image to a file with a chosen name using the -o flag.

brief.install_notes: Install the Rust programming language first, then run cargo install codevis. On Linux you may need to add cargo's binary folder (/home/username/.cargo/bin/) to your PATH if it is not already there. The Homebrew formula has no extra caveats. No accounts or special hardware are mentioned.
brief.standout: It turns a whole codebase into a single picture that shows structure and file sizes at a glance, rather than a file tree or a stats table. The readable mode lets the same image be zoomed into and read.
brief.status: unknown. The README has no release dates, changelog, or commit information, and I did not check the repository's commit history or releases page.
brief.caveats: The image shows shape and size, not the exact characters, unless you use the readable mode and zoom in. Only UTF-8 encodable files are included. Installation requires building from source with Rust and cargo, which may take time. The README does not state a license.
